elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 27.3 states that the Agreement “shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York.”

elements.element: Disputes arising under or in connection with the Agreement are subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: Section 27.3 provides that the Parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state courts located in New York County for such disputes.

elements.element: Disputes arising under or in connection with the Agreement are subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: Section 27.3 provides that the Parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal courts located in New York County for such disputes.

elements.element: The Agreement is governed by one of the permitted fallback laws: Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales law.

elements.element: The selected courts correspond to a permitted fallback package: Delaware courts with Delaware law, California courts with California law, or London courts with the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects state and federal courts in New York County rather than Delaware courts, California courts, or courts in London.

result.reason: The added operative language fully implements the preferred New York governing-law and exclusive-forum position. It does not implement any fallback package, but no fallback is needed because the preferred position is satisfied. The addition is narrowly directed to governing law and forum, and existing Section 27.2 can coexist with the express choice in Section 27.3.
